questions.question: What is the definition of a process?
options: A passive entity stored on a disk
questions.explanation: A process is an active entity defined as a program in execution, whereas a program on disk is a passive executable file.

questions.question: Which section of a process's memory layout contains dynamically allocated memory?
questions.explanation: The Heap section holds memory that is dynamically allocated during process run time.

questions.question: Which section contains global variables?
questions.explanation: The Data section stores global and static variables, while the Text section holds code and the Stack holds temporary local data.

questions.question: What state is a process in when instructions are being executed?
questions.explanation: A process is in the Running state when its instructions are actively being executed on a CPU core.

questions.question: When a process is waiting for an I/O event to occur, it is in which state?
questions.explanation: A process enters the Waiting state when it cannot continue until some external event (such as I/O completion or a signal) occurs.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT stored in the Process Control Block (PCB)?
questions.explanation: The PCB stores process-specific context such as process state, program counter, CPU registers, scheduling data, memory limits, and I/O status, not the network interface's hardware MAC address.

questions.question: What is the set of processes residing in main memory, ready and waiting to execute called?
questions.explanation: Processes that are in main memory and ready to run on the CPU are kept in the Ready queue.

questions.question: What occurs when the CPU switches from one process to another?
questions.explanation: Switching the CPU to another process requires saving the current process's state and loading the saved state of the next process, known as a context switch.

questions.question: Context switch time is considered to be:
questions.explanation: Context switch time is pure overhead because the system performs no useful application execution while saving and restoring PCB state.

questions.question: In Android, which process type is considered the least important and is terminated first to reclaim resources?
questions.explanation: Android places Empty processes at the bottom of its importance hierarchy, terminating them first when system resources must be reclaimed.

questions.question: What UNIX system call creates a new process?
questions.explanation: In UNIX systems, the fork() system call creates a new child process by duplicating the parent's address space.

questions.question: What UNIX system call is used after a fork to replace the process' memory space with a new program?
questions.explanation: The exec() system call loads a binary file into memory and replaces the calling process's memory image with the new program.

questions.question: What is a process called if it has terminated but its parent has not yet invoked the wait() system call?
questions.explanation: A process that has finished execution but whose exit status has not yet been collected by its parent via wait() is a Zombie process.

questions.question: What is a process called if its parent terminates without invoking wait()?
questions.explanation: When a parent process terminates before waiting for its child processes, those remaining children are called Orphan processes.

questions.question: Google Chrome Browser uses a multiprocess architecture. Which process manages the user interface, disk, and network I/O?
questions.explanation: In Chrome's multiprocess architecture, the Browser process manages the user interface as well as disk and network I/O, while Renderer processes render web pages in sandboxes.

questions.question: Which model of Interprocess Communication (IPC) involves a region of memory that is shared by cooperating processes?
questions.explanation: In the Shared memory IPC model, cooperating processes establish a shared region of memory and exchange data by reading and writing to it.

questions.question: In the Producer-Consumer problem, which variation places no practical limit on the size of the buffer?
questions.explanation: An Unbounded-buffer places no practical limit on buffer size, so the producer never has to wait for buffer space.

questions.question: In a shared-memory solution for a bounded buffer of size BUFFER_SIZE, how many elements can actually be used to store items correctly?
questions.explanation: The circular array implementation using only in and out pointers distinguishes full from empty by leaving one slot unused, allowing at most BUFFER_SIZE - 1 items.

questions.question: Message passing IPC provides which two primary operations?
questions.explanation: Message-passing facilities provide at least two operations: send(message) and receive(message).

questions.question: In direct communication, what must processes do?
options: Use exactly the same memory space
questions.explanation: Under direct communication, each process that wants to communicate must explicitly name the recipient or sender of the communication.

questions.question: In indirect communication, messages are directed to and received from:
questions.explanation: With indirect communication, messages are sent to and received from mailboxes (also referred to as ports).

questions.question: Blocking message passing is considered:
questions.explanation: Blocking send or blocking receive is considered synchronous because the sender waits until the message is received or the receiver waits until a message is available.

questions.question: If both send and receive are blocking operations, the scenario is known as a:
questions.explanation: When both send() and receive() are blocking, the sender and receiver synchronize directly in a rendezvous.

questions.question: A message queue attached to a link with "Zero capacity" means:
options: The sender must wait for the receiver (rendezvous)
questions.correctAnswer: The sender must wait for the receiver (rendezvous)
questions.explanation: A zero-capacity queue cannot store any messages waiting on the link, so the sender must block until the receiver receives the message.

questions.question: Which IPC mechanism relies entirely on the operating system for communication?
questions.explanation: Message passing is mediated by the kernel via system calls for every transfer, whereas shared memory only requires kernel intervention to establish the shared region.

questions.question: A program becomes a process when an executable file is loaded into memory.
questions.explanation: A program is a passive executable file on disk that becomes an active process once loaded into memory.

questions.question: The stack and heap sections of a process memory layout remain fixed in size during execution.
questions.explanation: Only the Text and Data sections are fixed in size; the Stack and Heap shrink and grow dynamically during program execution.

questions.question: The wait() system call takes a process out of the ready queue until the child process terminates.
questions.explanation: Calling wait() blocks the parent process and moves it out of the ready queue until the child terminates.

questions.question: In a bounded buffer message passing queue, the sender never waits.
questions.explanation: In a bounded-capacity queue, the link has finite length n; if the queue is full, the sender must block until space becomes available. Only in an unbounded queue does the sender never wait.

questions.question: A context switch does no useful work while switching.
questions.explanation: Context switch time is pure overhead because the system does no useful application work while saving and loading process states.
